sections.value:
Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #288, exact head 2a38673f47d08acf6ecba8c7ad06a1000ab980af; reviewed against bc1ca834aa1163f86780f77bd83036f3b6b4e6ef. No introduced security vulnerability or normal-use security blocker found in the eight-file diff. Graded under current C21, C25, C33 and C34.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|

No vulnerability rows.

Requested checks

- Attach lock, crates/tmux/src/control.rs:476-518: the server label is restricted to alphanumerics, hyphen and underscore before joining the state root. Creation requests 0600. Metadata and permission narrowing use the opened File, not a second pathname lookup; the PR does not unlink or replace the inode before try_lock. This avoids a pathname check/chmod race and preserves an existing holder's lock identity. OpenOptions still follows symlinks: there is no O_NOFOLLOW or ownership/ancestor-permission attestation in this code. That path-open behavior is inherited, not a new claim of symlink protection. A different-account symlink/path-substitution exploit would require write/replace access to the configured state-root path; hostile same-user path mutation is outside C33. Mode narrowing also does not revoke descriptors another account opened before the repair. These are explicit limits, not newly found blocking vulnerabilities; no cross-account exploit was demonstrated.
- Snapshot cleanup, harness/scripts/release-build.sh:42-54,81-99: snapshot is initialized empty and then assigned only from mktemp -d. rm receives the exact quoted owned directory, with no wildcard, evaluation or path concatenation in cleanup. The empty-path check is a one-directional deletion brake, not a retention policy. Successful handoff clears ownership. Failed removal is reported. EXIT cleanup preserves the build/signal exit, and the HUP/INT/TERM traps wait for the foreground child before cleanup. This is not authentication of an arbitrarily hostile TMPDIR; environment and executable selection remain within the trusted-user boundary. No real deployment or recursive deletion was performed by this review.
- Niceness, harness/scripts/nice19.sh:16-39: /bin/ps is the default absolute executable; nonzero status and malformed output refuse before the requested command runs. Whitespace trimming and the nested digit check reject empty, bare-minus, range, word, repeated-minus and multi-line values. Negative integers work. Both exec paths retain the original argument boundaries. NICE19_PS is a trusted test seam, not a remote-input surface.
- Embedded inputs, harness/scripts/release-build.sh:62-68: the six actual include_str hook paths, .dd/schemas/pij and templates/roles are covered by the tracked/untracked dirty-input check. Both fixture helpers and their script environments use the hermetic Git configuration flags.
- Process safety, AGENTS.md:106: the rule forbids pattern-based killing and permits only the PID or process group of a job the agent started. It does not authorize killing other seats' matching processes.
- Privacy: the complete diff was inspected; the helper's added-line scan found no credential-pattern or private-home-path match. No secrets or C21-forbidden private identities/paths were identified in the changes. The pattern scan is supporting evidence, not a complete secret detector.

Evidence and proof grade

- just pr-freeze 288: passed at the exact head, with main/CLEAN, non-draft, latest checks successful, no added migrations, and successful exact-head Delivers CI. The detached checkout remained clean.
- Delegated local nice -n 19 python3 - probes: 15/15 niceness checks, exit 0; seven exact cleanup-block checks, exit 0; embedded-input/privacy/hermetic-Git assertions, exit 0. These receipts were recovered from the completed helper tool events, not inferred from its verdict-only response. Cleanup rm was mocked; signal probes targeted only the child PID they started. The cleanup probe validates the extracted exact block, not a fresh end-to-end cargo build.
- Helper syntax/diff checks: /bin/bash -n harness/scripts/release-build.sh; /bin/sh -n harness/scripts/nice19.sh; git diff --check bc1ca834 HEAD completed without reported errors.
- Exact-head CI run 44720859714, check (22) job 136238448733: release-build.test.ts 6 passed, shared-build.test.ts 23 passed, nice19.test.ts 11 passed; full TS 2375 passed, seven skipped; audit-gate reported no unallowed high findings. Node 24 check and Rust lint also succeeded.
- Successful Rust retry job 136238446465: 2654 passed, six skipped. Selected artifact 14621972912 from that successful job's upload log, not by the reused junit-linux name. Zip SHA-256: 8d8ff283524c0a67fea57c2dd18702c56101816ba815283f8363bef67184baa5. JUnit confirms the_attach_lock_is_private_and_narrowed_in_place PASS and separate_adapters_cannot_both_reserve_one_pane PASS. The earlier F237 fixture failure remains separate; no evidence here ties it to the permission change.
- Local harness boot returned ready:false for missing dependencies; just local-path-check could not find tsx (127). No dependencies were installed or symlinked, no local Cargo build was started, and no live deploy or shared OMP settings probe was performed. Local full harness checks were not run; this is a security review verdict, not a claim that author/merge gates were rerun locally. The PR's earlier local harness-check receipt is not presented as an exact-head local rerun.

Cost scope: no new loop, poll, timer or per-seat launch. Existing niceness measurement remains one /bin/ps per invocation; cleanup is once per exit; lock repair adds descriptor metadata and conditional chmod work per attach. Live before/after cost certification belongs to the performance role, not this verdict.

Harness feedback (nonblocking): difficulties were dependency-free review readiness and a verdict-only helper response despite requested evidence. magicWand: return structured file/line and command/result receipts even when the vulnerability list is empty, with an explicit CI-only/local-unavailable proof grade. The completed tool-event recovery preserved evidence without repeating the code review.

Retaining security/288 until merge, including after this verdict. No product files changed.
